clues: This city lies on a river in the very centre of a broad peninsula in south west Europe. Dry plains stretch out around it on all sides.
This high city far from the sea gets the least rain of any capital on its continent. Yet its winters still bring frost, and now and then snow.
A walled fort town stood here for ages before kings took much note of it. In 1561 the king moved his court here for good, and rule stayed.
A statue of a bear by a strawberry tree stands on the east side of the Puerta del Sol. That pair is the coat of arms of this city, its proud badge.
Spain's king has his great palace in this city, and the national government runs the land from here. It is the political heart of the whole country.
